verifier_owned_fixture.scenario: Call G1->G2 overlap twice with the same acknowledged state fingerprint after first SHIFT_COMPLETE.
verifier_owned_fixture.observed: Second and third calls both return SHIFT_COMPLETE with identical output; no shift_id/transfer token/consumed handoff fingerprint or durable transfer state exists to reject replay.
verifier_owned_fixture.expected: After one receiver ACK and torque transfer, replay of the same handoff must be rejected or deterministically return ALREADY_TRANSFERRED without authorizing duplicate execution.

root_cause: overlap_shift is stateless with respect to completed transfer and treats any matching receiver_state_fingerprint as a fresh valid completion.
The success requirement explicitly forbids duplicate execution after ACK, but the candidate has no single-transfer idempotency/consume guard.
repair_acceptance: Introduce a deterministic shift/transfer identity bound to mission_id, step_id, from_gear, to_gear, state_fingerprint and handoff sequence/nonce.
Persist or pass an authoritative consumed-transfer set/token state so an acknowledged transfer can complete exactly once.
Replay of the same completed transfer must be rejected or return a non-executing ALREADY_TRANSFERRED result.
Add tests for duplicate ACK/replay, stale ACK after state-fingerprint change, and ACK for a different shift identity.
Keep existing RPM preservation, compact no-raw-chat handoff, lower-guard-first downshift, three-slot topology, storage and progress protections unchanged.
